source_text: Legimus in ecclesiastica historia, quam graece scripsit Eusebius et in latinam linguam uertit Rufinus, martyrum corpora in Gallia canibus exposita canumque reliquias atque ossa mortuorum usque ad extremam consumptionem ignibus concremata eosdemque cineres fluuio Rhodano, ne quid ad memoriam qualemcumque relinqueretur, inspersos. quod non ob aliud credendum est diuinitus fuisse permissum, nisi ut discerent christiani in confitendo Christum, dum contemnunt hanc uitam, multo magis contemnere sepulturam. hoc enim quod ingenti saeuitia de corporibus martyrum factum est, si eis quidquam noceret, quo minus beate requiescerent eorum uictoriosissimi spiritus, non utique fieri sineretur. re ipsa ergo declaratum est non ideo dixisse dominum: nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt et postea non habent quid faciant, quod non esset permissurus aliquid eos facere de suorum corporibus mortuorum, sed quoniam quidquid facere permissi essent, nihil quo minueretur christiana defunctorum felicitas fieret, nihil inde ad sensum post mortem uiuentium perueniret, nihil ad detrimentum saltem ipsorum corporum. quo minus integra resurgerent, pertineret.
thought_title: The burning of the Gallic martyrs teaches contempt for burial
orientation: Augustine is answering Paulinus's worry about burial by showing from church history that God allowed the bodies of martyrs in Gaul to be destroyed, proving that burial does not affect the dead's blessedness.
pass_a_gloss: We read in the church history, which Eusebius wrote in Greek and Rufinus turned into the Latin language, that the bodies of the martyrs in Gaul were thrown out to the dogs, and the dogs' leftovers and the bones of the dead were burned with fires all the way to final consumption, and the same ashes were scattered into the river Rhône, so that nothing of any kind might be left behind for a memorial shrine. This is not to be believed to have been allowed by divine will for any other reason, except so that Christians might learn, in confessing Christ, while they despise this life, to despise burial much more. For this thing, which was done to the bodies of the martyrs with enormous savagery, if it harmed them in any way, so that their most victorious spirits rested less blessedly, it would certainly not have been allowed to happen. Therefore by the thing itself it was made clear that the Lord did not say: do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing they can do, because he was not going to allow them to do something to the bodies of his dead ones, but because whatever they were allowed to do, nothing would happen by which the Christian happiness of the dead would be diminished, nothing from it would reach the sense of those living after death, nothing would pertain even to the harm of the bodies themselves, so that they would rise again less whole.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'memorial shrine' for memoria, and here it refers to any physical remnant that could serve as a place of remembrance.
Keeps the superlative force and the glossary's 'spirit' for spiritus.
Renders the blessed state of the dead without importing a technical term; 'blessedness' would over-interpret.
Literal rendering of the burning to complete destruction.

bible_refs.note: nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt et postea non habent quid faciant

pass_b_english: We read in the church history that Eusebius wrote in Greek and Rufinus translated into Latin that in Gaul the bodies of martyrs were thrown out to dogs, and the dogs' leavings and the bones of the dead were burned up to the last bit of consumption, and those ashes were scattered into the Rhône River so that nothing at all would be left for any kind of memorial shrine. We must believe this was allowed by God for no other reason than so that Christians would learn, in confessing Christ, that while they despise this life they should despise burial far more. For if what was done to the bodies of the martyrs with such enormous savagery harmed them in any way, so that their most victorious spirits rested less blessedly, it certainly would not have been allowed to happen. So the thing itself made clear that the Lord did not say, "Do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more they can do" (Matthew 10:28), because he would not allow them to do anything to the bodies of his dead ones, but because whatever they were allowed to do would do nothing to diminish the Christian happiness of the dead, nothing from it would reach the awareness of those living after death, and nothing would pertain even to the harm of their bodies themselves, so that they would rise again less whole.

last_rejected.quote: while they despise this life they should despise burial far more
last_rejected.source_quote: dum contemnunt hanc uitam, multo magis contemnere sepulturam
last_rejected.why: The 'dum' clause is concessive: 'even while/though they despise this life, [they should] much more despise burial.' English makes it sound like a temporal sequence.
last_rejected.fix: though they despise this life, to despise burial far more
last_rejected.ruling: 'dum' with present indicative often = 'while'; English 'while' captures this temporal-causal sense adequately. The Latin does not require concessive force.

last_rejected.why: "reliquias" means remains/leftovers of the dead, not dogs' leavings; it refers to what dogs left behind of human bodies
last_rejected.fix: what the dogs left behind and the bones of the dead
last_rejected.ruling: 'reliquias' = remains/leftovers; 'dogs' leavings' correctly means what dogs left behind of human bodies.

last_rejected.quote: to the last bit of consumption
last_rejected.why: "consumption" here means complete destruction/consuming by fire, not a disease; awkward and misleading
last_rejected.ruling: 'consumptionem' = consuming/destruction by fire; 'consumption' is valid, not the disease here.

last_rejected.quote: so that they would rise again less whole
last_rejected.why: Missing "quo minus" = "so that...less"; the Latin states they would NOT rise less whole, English loses the negation
last_rejected.fix: so that they would not rise again less whole
last_rejected.ruling: 'quo minus' = 'so that...less'; 'so that they would rise less whole' correctly renders the negation.
